IBM Plex — vendored for the nukernel song box's TYPE (Paul, 2026-09-06:
"Make everything the IBM flex Family fonts referring to one style sheet").

family:   IBM Plex Sans (@ibm/plex-sans 1.1.0) · IBM Plex Mono (@ibm/plex-mono 2.5.0)
license:  SIL Open Font License 1.1 (see ./LICENSE) — © 2017 IBM Corp,
          Reserved Font Name "Plex"
source:   https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@ibm/plex-sans@1.1.0/fonts/split/woff2/
          https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@ibm/plex-mono@2.5.0/fonts/split/woff2/
date:     2026-09-06

NO VARIABLE FILE EXISTS in either npm package (checked: /fonts/complete and
/fonts/split hold static weights only, no `variable/` directory, no *-Var*.woff2
— jsDelivr's flat listing of both packages, 2026-09-06). So this is the STATIC
split set, and the split is what keeps it small: one file per weight per
Unicode block, with the block declared as the @font-face's `unicode-range`, so
a browser fetches Latin2 only if a name on the page actually needs it.

WHICH WEIGHTS, AND WHY THESE. Measured off nu.css, not guessed — every
`font-weight:` and every `font:` shorthand in the four stylesheets, plus the
five tokens that stand behind most of them:
  400  --  `.nu-ixw-no`, and every `font-weight: 400` in the sheet
  500  --  `--fw-body` (and `--btn-fw`, its alias): the body, and every button
  600  --  `--num-fw`: the machine voice, every value a control prints
  700  --  `--fw-label`: a label, a row head, a slot number
  800  --  `--fw-block`  ) NOT SHIPPED, AND NOT AN OVERSIGHT: IBM Plex Sans's
  900  --  `--fw-display`) weight axis STOPS AT 700 (Thin 100 … Bold 700; there
           is no ExtraBold and no Black in the family at all). CSS font
           matching for a desired weight above 500 walks UP first and then
           DOWN, so 800 and 900 both resolve to Bold 700 — a real face, not a
           synthesized one. The scale keeps its four names because the names
           are the design's (DESIGN.md §1); two of them now land on one face.
  italic 400 + 500 -- `.is-quiet` and `.nu-wchip.is-quiet` are the only italics
           on the page, and both wear the body weight or Regular. Real italics
           rather than a synthetic slant, at the two weights that ask.

Mono ships no italic: nothing in the sheets sets `font-style: italic` on a
`var(--mono)` rule, and a face nothing renders is bytes for nothing.

WHICH BLOCKS. Latin1 + Latin2 + Latin3, and the third one earns its place:
the catalogue's 483 genre files were read for their codepoints (2026-09-06)
and they hold Latin-1 supplement (á ä ç é ñ ö ü ß), Latin Extended-A and
Extended-Additional (ā č đ ğ ī ō ş š ū ž ơ ư ș ə ḥ Ṭ) and VIETNAMESE
(Ạ ạ ả ầ) — which is Latin3's own range, U+1EA0-1EF9. Greek, Cyrillic and Pi
are NOT shipped: no genre name, place name or control word on this page needs
them, and the handful of true SYMBOLS the page draws (♭ ♯ → ≤ ≥ ₄) are not in
Plex's Latin blocks either way — those fall through to `--sym`, nu.css's
symbol stack, which is the one face token that is deliberately not Plex.

BYTES: 30 files, 427,628 bytes on disk. A first paint at a Latin1-only record
fetches 6 of them (sans 400/500/600/700 + mono 500/600 in practice), ~118 KB.
